panels.armies.help:
Click an army to take command (issue orders in the detail panel on the left).
Ctrl+click to select multiple armies, then merge them in the bar at the top; merging requires every selected army to be idle and out of battle, with a combined total of no more than {{regimentCap}} regiments.
Turn on the gear beside the title for global auto-management: the panel locks and the AI moves, attacks and merges for you. Turn it off to manage individual armies with the small gear beside their status pill.
Armies rout when organization drops below 15; organization recovers each turn based on [[supply]].
The inline tag shows the composition: unit types and regiment count.
panels.armies.autoHelp:
When enabled, your armies move, attack and merge with nearby small armies automatically each turn, just like AI nations.
The army panel is unavailable during global auto-management; once you turn it off with the gear beside the title, the small gear beside a status pill manages one army individually.
Turning off auto-management immediately restores manual command of every army.

panels.armyDetail.help:
Select regiments and click Split to form a new army in an adjacent empty province; to merge, move into a friendly province or Ctrl+multi-select armies in the list on the right.
Organization recovers each turn from [[supply]] and armies rout below 15; unpaid upkeep lowers organization across the whole army.
Declare war before attacking an adjacent enemy province; the power comparison on the button is estimated from attack/defense and terrain.
Strategic redeployment withdraws an idle army to the rear; Wait ends this turn's action.
Disbanding an army demobilizes its regiments and cannot be undone.
Auto-managed armies can only be viewed; click "Stop auto-managing" to resume manual command.

panels.deploy.help:
Drag a unit type onto one of your map provinces to raise one regiment immediately; hover the same province for 2 seconds to keep recruiting until you release or run out of resources/cap.

Each regiment costs [[funds]] and [[industry]], never population; national army capacity scales with population and conscription policy, and a province holds at most 12 regiments.

Province stance: Auto (attack only with an edge), Defend (passive only), Attack (seek the weakest hostile neighbour). Neighbouring provinces coordinate on the same target without moving troops.

"Clear field troops" removes every field regiment and keeps the garrison.

panels.diplomacy.help.body:
Goal: annex every rival through war and peace treaties.
Losing your capital does not destroy a nation; only the loss of all formal territory does.

Effective control is not formal ownership; wars are fought province by province, and capturing a state capital or the national capital does not transfer the whole state.
Goal peace deals transfer only the agreed territory; a white peace returns temporary occupation on both sides and transfers no third-party land.
To declare war, first claim a state on the Expansion tab, then prepare a Conquest or Annexation goal; once it is ready, click Declare War to choose a war goal.

panels.expansion.help:
Claims are made per state: pay {{cost}} political power to file one, without changing control, legal ownership or historical cores; war justifications are created on the Diplomacy tab. The map has switched to state mode, and claimed states are tinted with our nation's color.

Click "Manage claims" to enter claim management: click a state marker on the map to add a claim, or mark an existing claim for cancellation; gold pulsing states are valid new targets. Press Esc to open a confirmation dialog, then confirm to submit all changes at once; cancelling keeps you in management mode.

You can declare war with a justification from the Diplomacy tab; claims involving an ongoing war cannot be cancelled.

panels.construction.help:
2 · After selecting a building, click one of your states on the map; for province buildings, click one of your provinces.
Each click adds one item; you can pick multiple sites in a row.
The map shows "built + in progress / cap": in-progress numbers are green and tiles under construction are overlaid in green; unavailable tiles are gray.
Color key: free / few / many / full; province buildings only show free / full.
Right-click or press Esc to cancel the current building selection.

State buildings affect only the state center and provinces belonging to the same state; province buildings are limited to one per province per type, with capacity numbers shown when zoomed in.
Construction consumes [[idle]][[factory]], at most 5 per project, assigned in queue order; surplus factories carry over. Construction pauses when there are no [[idle]][[factory]].
Cancelling an unfinished project refunds half of the resources paid.

panels.construction.factory.tooltip:
[[production]] {{prod}} · [[idle]] {{idle}} · total {{total}}

Scroll up to shift to [[production]]; down to shift to [[idle]].
You can also drag the slider, use arrow keys, or click the − / + buttons.

[[production]][[factory]] generate [[funds]] and [[industry]]; [[idle]][[factory]] are assigned to construction in queue order, up to 5 per project, each providing a base [[construction:0.5]]/[[turn]].
Output also depends on the source state's [[infrastructure]], while construction is multiplied by the target state's speed; assign high-output factories to production first.
With no [[idle]][[factory]], construction pauses.
panels.construction.effects.infrastructu:
L is the state [[infrastructure]] level (0–8):
[[factory]] output (including [[idle]]) = 80% + 5% × L
Construction speed = 80% + 5% × L
Army [[movement]] cost = 100% − 5% × L
[[supply]] efficiency = 100% + 5% × L
Only applies to provinces held by the same side as the state center.
